Original data:Passenger Lists, 1865–1935. Microfilm Publications T-479 to T-520, T-4689 to T-4874, T-14700 to T-14938, C-4511 to C-4542. Library and Archives Canada, n.d. RG 76-C. Department of Employment and Immigration fonds. Library and Archives Canada Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.

Name is found in St. Nicholas Ukrainian Catholic Church records as "Lechiw".

     Dmytro left the port of Antwerp onboard the 5340 ton SS Lake Michigan on March 23, 1910 at the age of 22 years (as being born in 1880). He was given as being single, never in Canada before, not reading or writing, and had Rail Road Contract # 97252. The ship arrived in St. John's New Brunswick on April 4, 1910 at 15:30 hours.

     Onboard the Lake Michigan were 1108 adults, and 171 children under the age of 14 years. Also onboard were his brother Wasyl Lechow, age 26, and (brother ?) Michael Lechow age 27. All of the Lechows were shown bound for Winnipeg, Manitoba. (Microfilm Roll # T4822).

     From the SS Lake Michigan Ship Manifest, Dmytro would have been born in 1888.  The date given for Dmytro's baptism on his church marriage records is given as 1891. The date of birth given on the tombstone in Elmwood Cemetery is given as "November 8, 1891- November 15, 1937. (3 years difference in age from that on the ship manifest).
     Dmytro's wife Catherine's age also differs by 1 year from the gravestone to that given on church records.

Refered to as "Danl Lecko", car repair CPR, and residing at 661 MagnusAve. in 1916,

Pitman for Street Railway in 1917,

"Motorman" residing at 661 Magnus Ave. in 1918,

Motorman for Street Railway in 1919,

Resided at 710 Burrows in 1920;

Motorman for Street Railway and residing at 457 Burrows in 1921,

Resided at 710 Burrows in 1922

Resided at 838 Alfred Avenue in 1926,

Employed with Winnipeg Electric in 1930 and 1935 and resided at 819 Aberdeen Avenue.

Place of birth is given at Helen's baptism as "Hutysko Ottwzya circ. Brody".

Daniel died in an accident in 1937, according to Walter Lechow, per telephone conversation of February 20, 1998 (possibly hit by a street car?).

Remembered as a "cousin" by Sam Lacho, but hte exact family relationship was not known.

Note:
Possible conflict in year of birth between ship's manifest and church marriage records.

From cemetery records: Catherine Lechow paid for her husband's grave on November 20, 1937.
